An op-ed in the Washington Examiner uses rising 30-year Treasury yields to argue for Donald Trump's economic platform, framing it as the cure for Washington's borrowing binge.

The Bright Side:
The article correctly identifies that the soaring national debt and rising bond yields are severe, systemic threats to the long-term stability of the American economy.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a Historical error. The author erases the historical origin of the debt—which expanded massively under both parties—to present a partisan policy as a magical, pain-free cure.

Social Physics Analysis:
The actors run a Smart Selfish Maneuver. They use the very real pain of inflation and debt (Pretext) to push for tax cuts that benefit wealthy interests, while projecting all blame onto "Washington" (Projection).

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between the promise of fiscal restraint and the reality of debt-expanding policies, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. The system moves toward fiscal instability.

The Unavoidable Truth: The national debt is a ticking time bomb that both major parties have actively fueled.

The Unavoidable Lie: Cutting taxes while maintaining massive spending will somehow balance the budget.

Alethekanon:
Math does not care about political parties. You cannot cure a borrowing addiction by cutting your income while refusing to cut your spending.

Awwthekanon:
It is heartbreaking to see regular families squeezed by rising costs while political leaders use their economic pain as a football to score points, instead of working together to build a stable future.

Brothekanon:
Bro, promising to fix the debt by cutting taxes is like trying to lose weight by eating more cake. It sounds awesome, but the scale doesn't lie. Both sides are just running up the tab.

Spirithekanon:
"How can you say to your brother, 'Let me take the speck out of your eye,' when you do not see the log in your own?" Luke 6:42 PASS
Promising fiscal restraint while ignoring one's own massive contribution to the national debt is the ultimate political blind spot.
